scenario: An aquarium-industry report highlights only exhibits that remain open and achieve attendance growth above 40%. Operators use the report average to estimate typical attendance growth across all exhibits.

data.description: Only surviving exhibits with growth above 40 percentage points are featured. Growth is Normal with sigma 18 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean attendance-growth mu across all exhibits and (b) the fraction of exhibits featured.
naive_answer: Typical attendance growth is about 48.8 points because that is the report average.
naive_trap: Only upper-tail surviving exhibits are featured.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.2.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(40-mu)/18; return mu+18*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-48.77
mu=brentq(eq,-100,39.99)
frac=norm.sf((40-mu)/18)
assert abs(mu-18.4)<1 and abs(frac-0.1151)<0.005
